idea: AI adoption programme for architecture practices
pain: AI is reshaping design workflow and practices have no strategy
v1: A workshop plus a 90-day rollout plan for one practice
verdict: Both careers at once and a warm channel, but architecture practices are famously poor buyers.

why.distribution: Her architecture peers are directly reachable and will take her call.
why.demand: Inferred. Practices are curious about AI but their margins make discretionary spend rare.
why.fmf: An architect who led AI adoption in a professional firm - the credibility here is unmatched.
why.defensibility: Her dual credibility is hard to copy; the programme content is not.
why.leverage: Programme materials reuse well across practices.
why.tailwind: AI is genuinely reshaping design workflow right now.
why.ceiling: £9k x 22 practices = £198k, but architecture practice budgets will not support this volume.

ceiling_arithmetic: £9k x 22 practices = £198k. Architecture practices run 5-15% margins and rarely spend £9k on consultancy; realistic conversion is 5-8 practices = £45-72k. The founder profile warns explicitly about this buyer.
carries: Unmatched credibility with a warm, directly reachable audience, on a genuinely urgent topic.
kills: Ceiling. Architecture practices are price-sensitive, low-margin buyers - the profile flags this specifically.
test: Quote £8k to three practice directors she knows.
test_pass: One books without asking for a discount.
test_fail: They want a free lunch-and-learn instead.
